name: cam_vf
description: C. jejuni virulence panel: T4SS virB, CDT, CiaB, GGT, T6SS Hcp and LOS-modification markers
note: Sixteen markers cut from public INSDC records: NCTC 11168 chromosome 1 NC_002163.1 (cdtA/B/C, ciaB, wlaN, the cgtA/neuA1 fusion), 81-176 plasmid pVir via AF226280.2 (virB4, virB11) and CP000550.1 (virB8/9/10), NCTC 13255 via LR134499.1 (ggt), the strain 108 T6SS locus JX436460.1 (hcp, annotated TssD), AF400048.1 (cstII) and AF130984.1 (cgtA OH4384 allele, cgtB). Sequences are byte-identical to the earlier locally-built panel except cgtB, strand-corrected here to the coding orientation of complement(5054..5959); annotations re-derived from INSDC so no third-party database terms ride the distribution. Screen-only; no typing scheme.

references.citation: Parkhill J, Wren BW, Mungall K, et al. The genome sequence of the food-borne pathogen Campylobacter jejuni reveals hypervariable sequences. Nature. 2000;403(6770):665-668.
references.note: NCTC 11168: cdtABC, ciaB, wlaN and the neuA1 fusion.

references.citation: Bacon DJ, Szymanski CM, Burr DH, Silver RP, Alm RA, Guerry P. DNA sequence and mutational analyses of the pVir plasmid of Campylobacter jejuni 81-176. Infect Immun. 2002;70(11):6242-6250.
references.note: The pVir T4SS virB panel (AF226280; virB8-10 on CP000550).

references.citation: Pickett CL, Cottle DL, Pesci EC, Bikah G. Prevalence of cytolethal distending toxin production in Campylobacter jejuni and related species. Infect Immun. 1996;64(6):2070-2078.
references.note: CDT prevalence and the cdtABC locus.

references.citation: Cheng J, Hyun J, Kapoor M, et al. Multifunctionality of Campylobacter jejuni sialyltransferase CstII: characterization of the beta-1,4-N-acetylgalactosaminyltransfer ase and alpha-2,8-sialyltransferase activities. Glycobiology. 2008;18(9):686-697.
references.note: CstII/cgtA LOS biosynthesis and ganglioside mimicry.

caveats: Marker presence is genetic potential, not virulence: CDT and T4SS genes can be partial or lost, and the LOS markers depend on phase variable homopolymer tracts not captured by presence screening.

cgtA is TWO records on purpose: the NCTC 11168 neuA1 fusion (1611 nt) and the OH4384 allele (1044 nt) — key on the accession when the distinction matters. cgtB is the coding strand of the OH4384 locus (strand-corrected from the earlier local panel, which stored the plus-strand slice; blastn is strand-agnostic so screening output is unchanged).

virB4/virB11 come from the original pVir submission (AF226280) and virB8/9/10 from the 81-176 genome project's re-annotation (CP000550): the two records differ by 5 bp overall, so cross-hits between the two virB source copies read near 100% identity.
cstII/cgtA/cgtB encode LOS ganglioside mimics (GM1/GD1a) associated with Guillain-Barre syndrome strains; absence of the gene does not exclude a mimicking LOS made by other alleles.
This panel does not replace C. jejuni/C. coli species identification (combine with the cpn60 or lpxA-based assays) or capsule typing (see cje_cps).
